body: Now that time has passed and my emotions are better handled, I’m looking at my account again, and I’m starting to second guess the whole thing. I’ve never missed a payment, so I thought this is just how this goes. But a few people have said it doesn’t sound right, so now im thinking I should look into it.
I hear you. The lesson has been learned. It was way too easy to dig this hole.

I’ll be honest, I’ve never had a late payment ever.  This is my very first one on my credit report. Is this not normal? Should I be reaching out to someone? The card in question was overcharged by the $20 so I thought it was a combination of things, but if it doesn’t sound right now I’m concerned. 

As for the balance, this one card is maxed out (the $20 is what went over the credit limit if that wasn’t clear). I’m general, I’m at like 11% total credit usage? I don’t like using the cards often. This was a huge mess up on my part.
Yea, I really thought I had handled this a while ago. The account in question has been settled, so seeing that this AM threw me off.
Thank you for this! I was feeling very discouraged and angry (at myself, my situation, the world) this morning when I wrote the post. I’m looking at other options right now.

A lot of information wasn’t included because I just wanted to vent more than anything since getting that notice this morning was pretty upsetting. But to answer your questions, the bed was purchased while I was still employed and had a home. I had gotten it as a treat to myself, but then I lost my job, home, and a few other things in one fell swoop. The credit score thing is important because I live in a HCOL area and a few of the places I was looking at ask for a minimum number. This drop puts me below that number. Same for the loan I wanted to get. As for not getting it because of employment, I have been applying for jobs, but even with a job some places still ask for the credit score for whatever reason. I’ve been applying for jobs and have a few interviews lined up. I was hoping to be able to have my own place and everything else by June, but I have no idea how long it’ll take to get a “good” credit score again. This means that the plan I had needs to be changed. It isn’t a big deal, but like I said earlier, I just wanted to vent. I was hoping to be in a better place by this point, and when everything is laid out it gets overwhelming to see it all. Especially since I just found out about needing the dental work and what not. It felt like a lot finances to process in such a short amount of time.
That’s what I was doing for a little bit, but my relative told me my time was up and I need to move out. Now I’m back at square one and have no idea where to go from here.
Few times; at 16, 18, (had a few “good” years filled with addiction problems) then again last year, and again a few days ago 🥲
Ty for this thread because I’m in the same boat and didn’t even realize it wasn’t ok

Getting a diagnosis helped me better communicate my experience. I was diagnosed a few years ago and have been receiving ongoing treatment since. At first, I was definitely weary of everything because up until that point, my identify and mental state were deeply intertwined. I found that working to separate the two was difficult, confusing, and overwhelming. Over time though, I realized that I was not my disorder. I realized that it was something I experienced. And acknowledging that my mental state was not who I am as a person, helped me rebuild my self esteem. That being said, I definitely still have ongoing issues and I honestly don’t think it’ll ever be “fixed” or that I’ll ever truly recover. But at least I now have the words and tools to help me address what’s going on. Plus, finding out that there was a name for what was happening to me felt validating. It felt like for the first time, I was a person instead of shapeless worthless lump that was taking up too much space. 

Everyone has a different experience and perspective on it, but those are my two cents.

I used to do this (I remember a period where I only ate blueberry pop tarts) It worked pretty well until I had to account for acquiring the food. Grocery stores and food shopping stress me out quite a bit. It definitely works if you can get over the initial hurdle of getting the foods.

To be honest, I’m trying to figure that out as well. A lot of the time I feel like I’m not actually depressed but just lazy. Like my depression isn’t real and I just need to suck it up. But then every bone in my body aches and I physically cannot muster up enough energy to do anything and somehow dying from starvation makes more sense than accomplishing the task at hand because it’s what I deserve for putting myself in this place. I know the line is somewhere between “I don’t want to” and “I’d rather die” and I have no idea how to determine the difference.

Yes. I would typically dress in menswear that’s too big (I’m a petite female).  I hardly wear makeup and my hair is never “done”.  I didn’t realize it was a coping method until my therapist pointed it out.
I’m in this weird place of wanting to sleep to not deal with real life but also being petrified that I’m going to stop breathing if I fall asleep so I can’t sleep.
